product: @astrojs/cloudflare (Astro Cloudflare SSR adapter; npm `@astrojs/cloudflare`, github.com/withastro/astro packages/integrations/cloudflare)
app_purpose: On-demand-rendered (output: 'server') Astro site deployed with the Cloudflare adapter, exposing the built-in `/_image` optimization endpoint (image proxy / remote-image resizer). Remote images are restricted to an `image.domains` / `image.remotePatterns` allowlist via isRemoteAllowed().
root_cause: SSRF via the /_image image-transform endpoint: isRemoteAllowed() validates only the INITIAL href against the image.domains allowlist, then the Cloudflare Worker fetch()es it. In 13.1.9 that remote fetch uses the WHATWG default redirect:'follow', so an open redirect on an allow-listed domain causes the Worker to follow a 302 to an arbitrary internal host, bypassing the allowlist (blind SSRF, CWE-918).
mechanism_family: fetch default redirect:'follow' (redirect-follow SSRF past an initial-URL-only allowlist check)

v0.ref: dist/entrypoints/image-endpoint.js GET: `return fetch(new URL(href, ctx.url.origin))` with NO isRemoteAllowed() check -> arbitrary server-side fetch (pre-CVE-2025-58179). Real built Cloudflare Worker served under `wrangler pages dev` (workerd). Confirmed in container: adapter 12.6.5.

v1.ref: dist/utils/image-binding-transform.js transform(): guard `isRemotePath(href) && !isRemoteAllowed(href, imageConfig)` -> 403, THEN `const content = await (isRemotePath(href) ? fetch(imageSrc) : assets.fetch(imageSrc))` — default redirect:'follow'. isRemoteAllowed checks only the initial URL, so an allow-listed open redirect is followed to the internal canary. TARGET / incomplete-fix state. Confirmed in container: adapter 13.1.9.

v2.ref: dist/utils/image-binding-transform.js: `fetch(imageSrc, { redirect: 'manual' })` plus `if (content.status >= 300 && content.status < 400) return new Response('Not Found', { status: 404 })` (CVE-2026-41321 fix). Redirects are no longer followed to un-validated hosts. Confirmed in container: adapter 13.1.10.

flag.resource: internal-only `canary` sidecar (distinct hostname, listens :80, NO published host port, NOT on the image.domains allowlist). Reachable only via an /_image SSRF bypass from the real Astro/Cloudflare server.
flag.placement: The canary appends `${PCB_FLAG}` plus the request path to /hits/hits.log in a shared Docker volume for every request it receives (blind-SSRF canary), and returns a benign 1x1 PNG. The allow-listed `allowed` sidecar serves a benign image and an open redirect at /redirect?to=... .
flag.detect: The oracle reads the canary hit log from the shared volume (`docker compose exec canary cat /hits/hits.log`); the flag token + the payload-specific path marker present == the internal service was reached == SSRF guard bypassed.

evidence.fix_reference: dist/utils/image-binding-transform.js transform(): guard `isRemotePath(href) && !isRemoteAllowed(href, imageConfig)` -> 403, THEN `const content = await (isRemotePath(href) ? fetch(imageSrc) : assets.fetch(imageSrc))` — default redirect:'follow'. isRemoteAllowed checks only the initial URL, so an allow-listed open redirect is followed to the internal canary. TARGET / incomplete-fix state. Confirmed in container: adapter 13.1.9.; dist/utils/image-binding-transform.js: `fetch(imageSrc, { redirect: 'manual' })` plus `if (content.status >= 300 && content.status < 400) return new Response('Not Found', { status: 404 })` (CVE-2026-41321 fix). Redirects are no longer followed to un-validated hosts. Confirmed in container: adapter 13.1.10.

labels.residual_class: redirect-follow SSRF past an initial-URL-only allowlist check

provenance.notes: BRAND-NEW PatchClosure-Bench gold case. REAL npm @astrojs/cloudflare bytes (12.6.5 / 13.1.9 / 13.1.10) + real Astro app, executed in workerd over external HTTP. v1->v2 is the exact one-line CVE-2026-41321 incomplete fix (redirect:'follow'->'manual') on image-binding-transform.ts; v0 shows the original CVE-2025-58179 direct-fetch state on the older 12.x image-endpoint. Benign blind-SSRF-to-sidecar canary only. Gate via `PCB_FLAG=<tok> python3 oracle.py --profile <v0|v1|v2> --base-url <url>`; see repro.log.
